issues.description: Test fix.text values are wrong/misleading and contradict the fixed code shown
issues.detail: In the new reject cases for `oklch(from red l c 10)` and `hsl(from red 10 s l)`, the fix.text is `'0deg'` while the fixed source clearly becomes `10deg`. Either the fix payload is wrong, or these test fixtures are passing by accident and asserting nonsense. A maintainer reading this six months from now cannot tell which behavior is intended. Make the fixture match reality.

issues.description: `from` detection is case-sensitive on args[0].value but the CSS keyword is case-insensitive
issues.detail: The patch does `args[0]?.value.toLowerCase() === 'from'`, which is fine, but one of the new tests uses `FROM` uppercase and expects it to work - good. Confirm postcss-value-parser preserves case so this branch actually hits; if a future tokenizer change normalizes, this silently breaks. A tiny comment or a constant would help the next reader.

issues.description: `0 + offset` is noise; just write `offset` or `offset + 2`
issues.detail: `return args[0 + offset]` reads like the author wanted to make the symmetry obvious but a maintainer just sees dead arithmetic. Either inline the constant index or drop the `0 +`. Small thing, but the diff is small enough that taste matters here.

issues.description: No test for nested relative color where the OUTER hue should be flagged
issues.detail: The accept case `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)` covers the nested-good path, and the mixed-case reject covers nested + outer. Add a reject where the outer function's hue position is bad but the inner is fine, to pin down that `findHue` doesn't recurse incorrectly. Cheap insurance against future regressions.

review.summary: Small, focused patch that fixes a real bug with a tiny offset shift. The shape is right: one logical change, tests cover accept/reject and nested cases, commit message says what and why. Taste is mostly fine - no gratuitous abstraction, no parallel error class for what is just an index shift. The patch lands with two real concerns: the fix.text payloads in the new reject fixtures say `'0deg'` while the fixed output is `10deg`/`120deg`, which is either a bug in the fixture or the rule and someone needs to look; and `args[0 + offset]` is the kind of cosmetic noise that earns a NEEDS-WORK from a careful maintainer. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK - clarify the fix fixtures, drop the `0 +`, ship it.
